text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: sustained RPM spike detected for model cobalt9b (hosted). Window: 03:12–03:18 UTC. 95th RPM = 3.2k, baseline = 420. Error rate up 0.7%. Suggested action: consider per-model RPM/TMP sculpting or routing to fallback variants. See dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/traffic?model=cobalt9b

elena: seeing this — paging oncall. any known deploys?

samir: not that i'm aware of. looks like a concentrated surge from a few API keys. pulling the key list now.

ops-bot: query results: top 3 API keys by tokens in window: api_ak_63 (34%), api_ak_12 (22%), api_ak_09 (8%). No enterprise SLA hits flagged yet.

arun: @elena if we don't throttle we'll burn through capacity and spike latency regionally. recommend a short RPM cap + TPM cap while we triage.

elena: agree. suggested quick mitigation: set rpm=60, tpm=12000 for cobalt9b, enable fallback to cobalt9b-lite (quantized) for non-enterprise plans. canary to 10% of traffic first.

morgan: i can flip the canary rule. samir — do you have the CLI or console command?

samir: use redwoodctl, example below. i'll prepare the exact command and roll it once we confirm owners.

samir: ```
# canary 10% traffic -> apply RPM/TPM cap for cobalt9b
redwoodctl traffic update --model cobalt9b --rpm 60 --tpm 12000 --canary 0.1 --scope hosted --reason "live mitigation - spike"
# fallback routing to cobalt9b-lite for non-enterprise plans
redwoodctl routing update --model cobalt9b --fallback cobalt9b-lite --scope hosted --condition "plan!=enterprise"
```

elena: copy. @morgan please confirm you can roll canary and watch latency dashboards. i'll notify support to prepare messaging if customers see degraded throughput.

morgan: rolling now — applying canary. watching realtime.

ops-bot: ACTION: applied canary 10% at 03:20 UTC. RPM/TMP caps set for canary group. Monitoring for 5m.

morgan: initial stats: canary showing 15% reduction in error spikes for routed requests, no latency regressions. overall system still high because remaining 90% unabated.

arun: let's escalate to 50% canary to get more relief while we collect customer list. proposing 50% for next 10m, then full 100% if stable. downside: more users see limited concurrency.

elena: call it — increase to 50%. samir, morgan, do it.

samir: executing: ```redwoodctl traffic update --model cobalt9b --rpm 60 --tpm 12000 --canary 0.5 --scope hosted --reason "escalate canary to 50%"```

ops-bot: ACTION: canary increased to 50% at 03:26 UTC. Monitoring for 10m.

morgan: telemetry: overall RPM dropped ~42%, latency P95 improved ~280ms -> 160ms, error rate down to 0.2%. Good signal.

elena: good. start assembling customer-impact list for those still affected (we need to know who is seeing throttled responses). samir, pull request logs by API key and classify by plan.

samir: pulled logs. affected keys in non-enterprise: api_ak_63 (high-volume bot), api_ak_12 (integration), many smaller keys. Enterprise keys are currently routed through reserved capacity and not impacted.

arun: recommend messaging for top 5 users (api_ak_63 discovery list). if they see 429s, direct them to increase plan or route to cobalt9b-lite.

elena: i'll coordinate support triage. @morgan keep the 50% canary for now; we'll only go to 100% if metrics remain stable for 10m.

morgan: noted. monitoring dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/observability/traffic?model=cobalt9b&view=canary

samir: small note: cobalt9b-lite has ~8% quality delta on long-contexts; we should avoid for customers doing long-doc summarization. cataloging affected customers that rely on long contexts.

elena: good catch. mark long-context customers as "no-auto-fallback" and only apply RPMS, not fallback routing for them. add to support ticket.

morgan: current telemetry at 03:34 UTC: metrics stable, error rate 0.18%, token spend down ~39%.

arun: propose we now set a global RPM cap for cobalt9b at 100 for non-enterprise plans (non-canary) and keep TPM at 12000, to avoid oscillations if spike restarts. That buys headroom.

elena: fine. do the change, but add an automatic rollback in 30m unless metrics improve. samir/morgan — record exact change in incident doc.

samir: applying global cap: ```redwoodctl traffic update --model cobalt9b --rpm 100 --tpm 12000 --scope hosted --condition "plan!=enterprise" --reason "post-mitigation steady cap"```

ops-bot: ACTION: global cap applied at 03:38 UTC for non-enterprise plans. Auto-rollback scheduled at 04:08 UTC unless canceled.

morgan: dashboard shows sustained improvement. can keep in place while we contact top customers.

elena: handoff in 20 minutes. @kai you'll pick this up — summarize state when you take over.

kai: taking next shift. i'll review logs, customer tickets, and telemetry. plan to maintain caps and escalate to Dedicated routing if required.

arun: leaving a note: had to block a small automated crawler (api_ak_63) by rate-limiting at gateway level; that recovered ~18% of capacity. manual mitigation details in incident doc.

elena: thanks all. action items: [samir] customer list + long-context flags, [morgan] monitor / cancel rollback if metrics unstable, [kai] follow up handoff + customer comms, [support] reach out to top 5 impacted.

support-bot: created ticket #INC-2026-412 for customer outreach.

kai: acknowledged. i'll take 03:40–07:40 UTC oncall. leaving a brief note in the rotation calendar. ping me if anything regresses. :white_check_mark:

elena: closing loop: incident mitigated by rate sculpting + crawler block. keeping caps until further notice. will produce a short postmortem with timeline.

ops-bot: thread closed for active paging at 03:50 UTC. reason: stable metrics and handoff complete.
